subject: Unit economics reconciliation — tokens per request, caching & batching clarifications
messages:
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@helixmed.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@helixmed.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Oct 2029 16:18:00 -0400
Subject: MAP + unit economics detail request (tokens, caching, batching)

Kim — thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to kick off a short MAP note focused specifically on unit economics so we can validate assumptions before legal/procurement spend time on the SOW. Quick asks below — can you confirm/attach the cost sims your team used?

High-level asks (we'll add to the MAP spreadsheet):
- Average tokens per API call you expect for our primary flows (summary extraction, one-pass QA, patient triage prompts) — please give P50/P95 if you have distribution.
- Caching behavior: what prefix/KV caching you recommend at our expected traffic patterns (10–20 TPS peak), and assumptions for cache hit rate (best/expected/worst).
- Batching: recommended max batch size and the latency impact (p50/p95) at 1, 5, 10 GPU backends.
- Fallback/quality tradeoffs: if we route to quantized model under load, what's the tokens/$ delta and estimated quality change?

We're trying to validate units-per-dollar in a conservative (procurement-friendly) way so legal can accept the MAP runway. If you can drop a short CSV of the simulation inputs and the MAP tab updated, that'd be ideal.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Price
Head of Product, HelixMed

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@helixmed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Oct 2029 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP + unit economics detail request (tokens, caching, batching)

Jordan — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a MAP workbook and the simulation CSV with conservative/expected/optimistic scenarios. Quick notes inline so procurement has something to cite in the MAP itself.

Summary (short):
- Tokens per call: P50 380 tokens, P95 980 tokens for the clinical summary flow; triage prompts average much lower (P50 120, P95 420). We instrumented these from the eval set you shared.
- Caching: recommend a two-layer approach — prefix caching at the request level (short-lived, 30s TTL for widgets) + KV cache for repeated context (30–90 minute TTL for session histories). Expected hit rates: optimistic 60% prefix / 45% KV; expected 40% / 30%; conservative 20% / 15%. Numbers in sheet column H.
- Batching: default batch target 16 tokens/sequence with dynamic batching window tuned to keep p50 latency under 150ms for 1–2 GPUs. At 10 GPUs we recommend target batch size 32 for throughput gains but note p95 latency increases ~120ms in our sims. Detailed latency vs batch-size table in workbook.
- Quantized fallback: switching to 4-bit quantized variants reduces inference cost ~35% on tokens/$ but test eval shows ~2–4 point BLEU/ROUGE delta on summary tasks — we flagged which prompts are sensitive.

Immediate asks back to you:
1) Can you confirm which flows we should treat as latency-critical (patient-facing) versus backend (async)? That changes prefetch & batch sizing.
2) For legal: do you want us to show both conservative and expected unit economics in the MAP, or only the conservative lane? Procurement historically asks for conservative numbers in the SOW but product prefers showing both.

I put an annotated MAP tab in the HLX_MAP_v1.3.xlsx. Karthik & Marissa — please review the conservative assumptions (sheet: "Procure conservative") and flag any redlines.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
Attachments: HLX_MAP_v1.3.xlsx, token-econ-sim-2029.csv, redwood-cost-playbook.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@helixmed.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Oct 2029 11:32:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP + unit economics detail request (tokens, caching, batching)

Adding ops/qa notes and one ask for the MAP: we ran a quick sensitivity matrix against the clinical-summary prompt set (sheet: "sensitivity-quick"). Key points: 
- The tokens/$ sensitivity is heavily driven by average prefix length — a 25% longer context (e.g., richer patient history) increases cost per summary ~18% in the expected sim.
- Cache hit-rate assumptions matter more than batch size for p95 cost if traffic is spiky. If Helix wants a tighter procurement guarantee at P95, we need to lock either (a) a minimum cache hit rate (via client-side dedupe/prefetch controls) OR (b) a committed reserved GPU buffer (Dedicated) to reduce fallback risk.

Suggested MAP language to close: 
- "Unit economics are modeled using three scenarios (conservative/expected/optimistic). Conservative assumes 20% prefix cache hit and quantized fallback during >85% backend saturation. Expected assumes 40% prefix hit with dynamic batching; optimistic assumes 60% prefix hit and 4-bit production quantization. See HLX_MAP_v1.3.xlsx, tab 'scenarios'."

Marissa — can you confirm the exact numbers we should put in the SOW appendix for tokens/$ at p50 and p95 for the conservative lane? I recommend we commit to a p50 tokens-per-dollar figure and mark p95 as "illustrative" unless Helix signs a dedicated commitment.

K
Karthik
Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@helixmed.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@helixmed.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Oct 2029 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP + unit economics detail request (tokens, caching, batching)

Kim, Karthik — this is great and aligns with what legal asked for. Quick decisions below so we can update the MAP and unblock SOW drafting: 
1) For MAP runway, procurement wants the conservative lane in the main SOW appendix and the expected/optimistic scenarios in an annex. That works.
2) We'll treat the patient-facing summary flow as latency-critical (p95 SLA target 300ms) — please call out any changes to batch sizing & prefetch needed to hit that SLA.
3) We're open to a short reserved buffer (2 GPUs peak) for the first 90 days if it buys down p95 risk. Can you provide a short cost addendum for that (monthly) and the change in units/$ at p95?

If you can drop an updated MAP tab with those two items (SOW conservative appendix row + reserved buffer addendum), procurement will move the draft to legal. Appreciate the clarity — Jordan
